_meta.purpose: Places where our output deliberately differs from the OCA published reference, so the weekly LLM judge stops reporting them and the auto-fix agent never 'corrects' them back.
_meta.why_this_file_exists: Since 2026-08-09 the auto-fix agent actually runs and opens pull requests. A recurring false positive is no longer just noise in a report — it is a PR that reverts a decision the parish made. A deliberate divergence has to be written down somewhere the judge reads.
_meta.bar_for_adding_an_entry: The divergence must be a decision someone made on purpose, with the reason recorded. A gap we have not got around to fixing is NOT a divergence — it belongs in the findings, where it will keep being reported until it is fixed.

divergences.ours: O Lord, we shall walk in the light of Thy countenance, and shall exult in Thy name forever.
divergences.reference: O Lord, we will walk in the light of Thy countenance, and will rejoice in Thy name forever.
divergences.why: The parish sings 'shall'. Confirmed by the choir director 2026-08-08. The OCA published text uses 'will'; this is a register choice, not an error, and it applies wherever this koinonikon is sung (Transfiguration and its afterfeast, and the Translation of the Image on 8-16).

divergences.ours: One Gospel — the Sunday-cycle reading only.
divergences.reference: Two Gospels on a polyeleos+ feast, e.g. 2026-08-16 lists Matthew 18:23-35 AND Luke 9:51-56; 10:22-24.
divergences.why: `opts.includeSecondGospel` defaults false, matching standard OCA parish practice of reading one Gospel even when the order appoints a second. It is a per-parish switch, not a bug. Both EPISTLES always render — epistle doubling is the norm — so a missing second Epistle IS a real finding.

divergences.ours: The Dismissal Theotokion of the resurrectional troparion's tone.
divergences.reference: Sometimes prints a different tone's Theotokion.
divergences.why: The Dismissal Theotokion is keyed by the tone of the resurrectional troparion actually sung, not by the reference's published tone column. Long-standing; previously carried as prose in the system prompt.
